memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Do not consider it a hardship to set your servant free, because their service to you these six years has been worth twice as much as that of a hired hand. And the Lord your God will bless you in everything you do. - Deut 15:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God addresses a subtle heart attitude here. When it came time to release a servant, the master might feel resentment — as if freeing them were a personal loss or hardship. But God says, "Do not consider it a hardship." Instead of grumbling over what releasing the servant might cost, the master was to recognize how much benefit the servant had already provided. God calls His people to a grateful, generous perspective rather than a grudging, calculating one.

This speaks to a common tendency in the human heart. We can focus so intently on what generosity costs us that we overlook all we have already received. We calculate the loss rather than counting the gifts. God invites a different way of seeing — one marked by gratitude rather than grievance, remembering how much good we have been given rather than resenting what we release.

This gracious perspective flows naturally when we remember God's own generosity toward us. Everything we have is a gift from His hand (1 Cor 4:7), so releasing and giving is really just passing along what we first received. When we grasp how abundantly God has blessed us, we hold things more loosely and give more freely, without the resentment that comes from thinking it all belongs to us. We should not read the closing promise of blessing as a prosperity guarantee, but as a reflection of how God delights to work through open-handed, grateful people. Ask God to free you from a grudging heart, and to give you a grateful perspective that gives freely and without resentment.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I focus on what generosity costs me, or on all I've already received?
- Where does resentment creep in when I'm called to give or release something?
- How does remembering God's abundant giving free me from a grudging heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, free me from a grudging, calculating heart that resents the cost of generosity. Help me remember how abundantly You have blessed me, holding things loosely and giving freely without resentment. Give me a grateful perspective that reflects Your generous heart. Amen.
